title: Zechariah 9 — The oracle against the nations and the king riding on a donkey

citations: Petersen, Zechariah 9-14 and Malachi (OTL, 1995), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed: maśśāʾ 'An oracle:' against ASV 'The burden'. The heading sense ('utterance', from nāśāʾ qôl) is standard, and the colon follows NRSV/NJPS. ʿên ʾāḏām is kept per MT, with the NRSV emendation reported.
wəḡam-ḥămāṯ tiḡbāl-bāh ṣōr wəṣîḏôn kî ḥāḵmâ məʾōḏ: exact.
wattiḇen ṣōr māṣôr lāh ...: exact; ṣōr/māṣôr pun noted.
hinnēh ʾăḏōnāy yôrišennâ ...: standalone ʾăḏōnāy 'the Lord' as in isaiah-woh. Exact.
wəyāšaḇ mamzēr bəʾašdôḏ ...: ASV 'a bastard' with NRSV 'mongrel people' in commentary. Exact.
wahăsirōṯî dāmāyw mippîw ... wəniš'ar gam-hûʾ lēʾlōhênû wəhāyâ kəʾallup̄ bîhûḏâ ...: exact; 'our God' (F1), 'chief' (central aluf).
wəḥānîṯî ləḇêṯî miṣṣāḇâ ...: MT min + ṣāḇāʾ 'against the army' (ASV) kept, revocalization reported. Exact.

citations: Meyers and Meyers, Zechariah 9-14 (AB 25C, 1993), ad loc.
Petersen, Zechariah 9-14 and Malachi (OTL, 1995), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed against ASV 'just, and having salvation'. nôšāʿ is a Niphal participle, and the passive 'delivered / given victory' (Deut 33:29; Ps 33:16) is the lexical value; 'victorious' is the HALOT Niphal gloss and the NRSV/NJPS word. ṣaddîq 'righteous' is its usual value. The one-animal parallelism is right, and the Matthew/John reception is noted. The reception note correctly says the TBWTT ch. 3 quotation omits ṣaddîq wənôšāʿ hûʾ, is labelled, and the line does not identify the king.

wəhiḵrattî (MT 1st person) kept with LXX 'he' reported; ʾap̄sê-ʾāreṣ 'the ends of the earth' is the universal idiom. Non-blocking fix: the note calls the dominion clause 'verbatim Ps 72:8', but Ps 72:8 reads wəyērd miyyām ʿaḏ-yām ..., a verb where Zechariah has the noun ûmošlô. Say 'nearly verbatim' or 'the second half is verbatim'.
gam-ʾatt bəḏam-bərîṯēḵ šillaḥtî ʾăsîrayiḵ mibbôr ʾên mayim bô: exact; central bor applied.
šûḇû ləḇiṣṣārôn ʾăsîrê hattiqwâ ... mišneh ʾāšîḇ lāḵ: exact.
kî-ḏāraḵtî lî yəhûḏâ qešeṯ millēʾṯî ʾep̄rayim ... ʿal-bānayiḵ yāwān: 'Greece' follows the English-name convention (daniel-woh), with Javan in commentary. Exact.
Disputed 'shofar' (ASV 'trumpet'), as at Zeph 1:16; source pointing yəhōwih with ʾăḏōnāy noted. 'whirlwinds of the south' (ASV) with Teman in commentary. Exact.
yāḡēn ʿălêhem wəʾāḵəlû wəḵāḇəšû ʾaḇnê-qelaʿ wəšāṯû hāmû kəmô-yāyin ...: ASV, with the obscurity and the LXX 'blood' reading in commentary. Exact.
wəhôšîʿām YHWH ʾĕlōhêhem ... ʾaḇnê-nēzer miṯnôsəsôṯ ʿal-ʾaḏmāṯô: exact; 'their God' (F1), 'his ground' (central adam-adamah).
kî mah-ṭûḇô ûmah-yop̄yô dāḡān baḥûrîm wəṯîrôš yənôḇēḇ bəṯulôṯ: exact, with the referent of 'his' left open as in the Hebrew.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked all 17 lines in the English alone. No English line reads as interpretation. The canon-cited verses (9:9 (with 9:10)) render the Hebrew at standard values, and each reception note is under its own 'Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim)' heading. Each note's quotation was verified against the canon text (TBWTT ch. 3 and ch. 5, FR/EN). Capitalisation (e.g. 'the Fish Gate') and vocabulary updates ('scroll', 'lampstand') are register or name conventions with lexical basis, not lens.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 109 LP1 lines, 31 overlay entries and 27 central ops were formed from the chapters, the sources, the drafts, the overlays and the diff, and recorded before wave-lp1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's watch points were each re-tested: Zeph 1:18 'earth', Zeph 1:10-11 names, Zech 4:14, Zech 9:9, Jer 10:5 and the unquoted Jer 10:2-5. The report does not mention the two Zech 4 speech-line issues (4:10 quote boundary; 4:13 'answered'), which stand as revise. The founder points F1-F5 are answered below.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-isaiah-aligned-conventions: Ratify for the Latter Prophets: 'God', 'earth'/'land' by scope, lowercase 'spirit', 'create' and 'oracle' are each the ASV/NRSV/NJPS-backed rendering and keep the five books one volume with Isaiah. Harmonize Ezekiel at its next wave, not by retro-editing signed-off chapters. The 'God'/'Elohim' split is the one item the reviewer flags for explicit founder ratification, because it is a project-stance choice.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-officials-shofar-vs-isaiah: Align Isaiah to 'officials' (Isa 32:1; 40:23; 43:28) and 'shofar' (Isa 27:13) at its next pass; both are lexically better grounded and already corpus rulings. Then promote megillah/menorah/sarim/shofar to central entries as the report proposes. Keep the Exodus 25 'lampstand' dependency on the Exodus checklist.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F3-neum-declares: Adopt 'declares YHWH' corpus-wide. Zechariah has ʾāmar YHWH (4:6) and nəʾum YHWH (5:4) within a few verses, and Isaiah's 'says' for both (e.g. ISA-14:22, checked) erases a distinction the Hebrew makes. Align Isaiah later.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-unquoted-messenger-formula: Ratify. At Jer 10:2-6 the Hebrew does not mark where the oracle ends, and leaving it unquoted avoids inventing a boundary. Related: at Zech 4:9-10 the wave's own marks run YHWH's word into the messenger's answer, which is the reviewer's revise at ZEC-WOH-4:10.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-sons-of-fresh-oil: Ship 'the two sons of fresh oil'. It is the most literal rendering, lexically grounded (yiṣhār, no māšaḥ), and inferred is the honest label; 'anointed ones' stays in commentary for reception continuity. If the founder wants a gentler line, 'the two sons of oil' (ASV margin) is the conservative literal fallback.

paragraphs.text: מַשָּׂ֤א דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חַדְרָ֔ךְ וְדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק מְנֻחָת֑וֹ כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ עֵ֣ין אָדָ֔ם וְכֹ֖ל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: An oracle: the word of YHWH upon the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be its resting place; for the eye of man and of all the tribes of Israel is toward YHWH;

notes.official: *maśśāʾ* 'An oracle' heads the two collections that close the book (9:1; 12:1) and the book of Malachi (Mal 1:1). It is rendered 'oracle' under the corpus ruling (`massa-oracle-latter-prophets`; isaiah-woh 13:1), replacing the draft's ASV 'burden', and set off with a colon, because *maśśāʾ* is a heading followed by the word it introduces (NRSV, NJPS). *dəḇar-YHWH bəʾereṣ ḥaḏrāḵ* 'the word of YHWH upon the land of Hadrach': Hadrach is Hatarikka, an Aramean city-state north of Hamath known from Assyrian records (central `eretz`). *kî laYHWH ʿên ʾāḏām wəḵōl šiḇṭê yiśrāʾēl* 'for the eye of man and of all the tribes of Israel is toward YHWH' (MT, ASV); others render 'YHWH has an eye on humankind', and NRSV emends to *ʿārê ʾărām* 'the cities of Aram'. The MT is kept (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zechariah-4-5-9`; `mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`). Chapters 9-14 are often called Second Zechariah and dated later than chs. 1-8 (Petersen, *Zechariah 9-14 and Malachi*, OTL, 1995). English name forms throughout (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וְגַם־חֲמָ֖ת תִּגְבָּל־בָּ֑הּ צֹ֣ר וְצִיד֔וֹן כִּ֥י חָֽכְמָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: and Hamath also, which borders on it; Tyre and Sidon, because she is very wise.

notes.official: Hamath, and the Phoenician cities Tyre and Sidon. *kî ḥāḵmâ məʾōḏ* 'because she is very wise', the commercial wisdom for which Tyre is mocked in Ezek 28:3-5.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּ֥בֶן צֹ֛ר מָצ֖וֹר לָ֑הּ וַתִּצְבָּר־כֶּ֙סֶף֙ כֶּֽעָפָ֔ר וְחָר֖וּץ כְּטִ֥יט חוּצֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And Tyre built herself a stronghold, and heaped up silver like the dust, and fine gold like the mire of the streets.

notes.official: *wattiḇen ṣōr māṣôr lāh* 'And Tyre built herself a stronghold', a play on *ṣōr* 'Tyre' and *māṣôr* 'fortress'. *ḥārûṣ* 'fine gold'.

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֤ה אֲדֹנָי֙ יֽוֹרִשֶׁ֔נָּה וְהִכָּ֥ה בַיָּ֖ם חֵילָ֑הּ וְהִ֖יא בָּאֵ֥שׁ תֵּאָכֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Behold, the Lord will dispossess her, and he will strike her power in the sea; and she shall be devoured with fire.

notes.official: *hinnēh ʾăḏōnāy yôrišennâ* 'Behold, the Lord will dispossess her': the standalone *ʾăḏōnāy* is rendered 'the Lord' (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`; as isaiah-woh 6:1). *ḥêlāh* 'her power' (ASV; NRSV 'her wealth'). Many commentators relate the oracle to Alexander's siege of Tyre in 332 BCE.

paragraphs.text: תֵּרֶ֨א אַשְׁקְל֜וֹן וְתִירָ֗א וְעַזָּה֙ וְתָחִ֣יל מְאֹ֔ד וְעֶקְר֖וֹן כִּֽי־הֹבִ֣ישׁ מֶבָּטָ֑הּ וְאָ֤בַד מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ מֵֽעַזָּ֔ה וְאַשְׁקְל֖וֹן לֹ֥א תֵשֵֽׁב׃

i18n.en: Ashkelon shall see it and fear; Gaza also, and shall writhe greatly; and Ekron, for her expectation shall be put to shame; and the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited.

notes.official: Four Philistine cities, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and Ashdod (v6), as in Amos 1:6-8 and Zeph 2:4. *mebbāṭāh* 'her expectation', what Ekron looked to, namely Tyre.

paragraphs.text: וְיָשַׁ֥ב מַמְזֵ֖ר בְּאַשְׁדּ֑וֹד וְהִכְרַתִּ֖י גְּא֥וֹן פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

i18n.en: And a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.

notes.official: *wəyāšaḇ mamzēr bəʾašdôḏ* 'And a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod': *mamzēr* (Deut 23:3) is a person of irregular or mixed birth, here perhaps a mixed population replacing the Philistines (NRSV 'a mongrel people'). The line keeps the ASV (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zechariah-4-5-9`).

paragraphs.text: וַהֲסִרֹתִ֨י דָמָ֜יו מִפִּ֗יו וְשִׁקֻּצָיו֙ מִבֵּ֣ין שִׁנָּ֔יו וְנִשְׁאַ֥ר גַּם־ה֖וּא לֵֽאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְהָיָה֙ כְּאַלֻּ֣ף בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְעֶקְר֖וֹן כִּיבוּסִֽי׃

i18n.en: And I will take away his blood out of his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth; and he also shall be a remnant for our God; and he shall be like a chief in Judah, and Ekron like a Jebusite.

notes.official: *wahăsirōṯî dāmāyw mippîw wəšiqquṣāyw mibbên šinnāyw* 'I will take away his blood out of his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth': the Philistine will give up meat eaten with its blood and unclean food (Lev 17:10-14; Isa 65:4; 66:17). *wəniš'ar gam-hûʾ lēʾlōhênû* 'and he also shall be a remnant for our God' (`elohim-god-latter-prophets`; the draft's 'our Elohim' followed the Genesis-scoped central entry). *kəʾallup̄ bîhûḏâ* 'like a chief in Judah' (central `aluf-edomite-clan-chief-tribal-confederation`, whose rationale names this verse); NRSV reads *ʾelep̄* 'a clan'. *wəʿeqrôn kîḇûsî* 'and Ekron like a Jebusite', the old population of Jerusalem absorbed into Judah.

paragraphs.text: וְחָנִ֨יתִי לְבֵיתִ֤י מִצָּבָה֙ מֵעֹבֵ֣ר וּמִשָּׁ֔ב וְלֹֽא־יַעֲבֹ֧ר עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם ע֖וֹד נֹגֵ֑שׂ כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְעֵינָֽי׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And I will encamp about my house against the army, against him who passes through and him who returns; and no oppressor shall pass through them any more; for now I have seen with my eyes.

notes.official: *wəḥānîṯî ləḇêṯî miṣṣāḇâ* 'And I will encamp about my house against the army': the MT is read as *min* + *ṣāḇāʾ* (ASV); NRSV and NJPS revocalize *maṣṣāḇâ* 'as a guard'. The MT is kept (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zechariah-4-5-9`; `mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`). *mēʿōḇēr ûmiššāḇ* 'against him who passes through and him who returns'. *kî ʿattâ rāʾîṯî ḇəʿênāy* 'for now I have seen with my eyes': YHWH's watchful eye (cf. 4:10).

paragraphs.text: גִּילִ֨י מְאֹ֜ד בַּת־צִיּ֗וֹן הָרִ֙יעִי֙ בַּ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם הִנֵּ֤ה מַלְכֵּךְ֙ יָ֣בוֹא לָ֔ךְ צַדִּ֥יק וְנוֹשָׁ֖ע ה֑וּא עָנִי֙ וְרֹכֵ֣ב עַל־חֲמ֔וֹר וְעַל־עַ֖יִר בֶּן־אֲתֹנֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; shout, daughter of Jerusalem! Behold, your king comes to you; he is righteous and victorious; lowly, and riding upon a donkey, even upon a colt, the foal of a donkey.

notes.official:
*gîlî məʾōḏ baṯ-ṣiyyôn* 'Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion': the city personified, summoned to greet its king. *ṣaddîq wənôšāʿ hûʾ* 'he is righteous and victorious': *nôšāʿ* is a Niphal participle, 'delivered, given victory' (Deut 33:29; Ps 33:16 'a king is not saved by a great army'). The line follows NRSV and NJPS ('victorious') and replaces the ASV's active 'having salvation', which goes back to the Old Greek *sōzōn* and the Vulgate *salvator*; *ṣaddîq* 'righteous' replaces ASV 'just' (overlay `tsaddiq-wenosha-ani-king-on-a-donkey-zechariah-9-9`). *ʿānî* 'lowly' (ASV) covers both 'poor, afflicted' and 'humble'. *ʿal-ḥămôr wəʿal-ʿayir ben-ʾăṯōnôṯ* 'upon a donkey, even upon a colt, the foal of a donkey' describes one animal in poetic parallelism (cf. Gen 49:11); Matt 21:2-7 reads two animals, John 12:14-15 one. 'donkey' replaces the ASV's 'ass' as a register update.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes 9:9-10 ('Rejoice ... O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee ... lowly, and riding upon an ass ... he shall speak peace unto the nations: and his dominion shall be from sea even to sea') as the creators' announcement of a Messiah who would spread to the whole world what only Israel knew. The canon's quotation omits the clause *ṣaddîq wənôšāʿ hûʾ*. The line renders the king's attributes at their lexical values and does not identify him.

paragraphs.text: וְהִכְרַתִּי־רֶ֣כֶב מֵאֶפְרַ֗יִם וְסוּס֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְנִכְרְתָה֙ קֶ֣שֶׁת מִלְחָמָ֔ה וְדִבֶּ֥ר שָׁל֖וֹם לַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּמָשְׁלוֹ֙ מִיָּ֣ם עַד־יָ֔ם וּמִנָּהָ֖ר עַד־אַפְסֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off; and he shall speak peace to the nations; and his dominion shall be from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.

notes.official: *wəhiḵrattî* 'And I will cut off' is the MT first person; the Old Greek has 'he will cut off', making the king the subject (NRSV). The MT is kept (`mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`). The disarming of Ephraim and Jerusalem (chariot, war-horse, battle bow) comes before the king's peace. *ûmošlô miyyām ʿaḏ-yām ûminnāhār ʿaḏ-ʾap̄sê-ʾāreṣ* 'and his dominion shall be from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth' is near-verbatim Ps 72:8, where the verb is the jussive *wəyērd* 'may he have dominion'. 'The River' is the Euphrates, and *ʾap̄sê-ʾāreṣ* 'the ends of the earth' is the universal idiom (`eretz-earth-or-land-latter-prophets`; isaiah-woh 45:22), replacing the draft's 'the ends of the land'. The canon quotes the verse with v9 (see the reception note there).

paragraphs.text: גַּם־אַ֣תְּ בְּדַם־בְּרִיתֵ֗ךְ שִׁלַּ֤חְתִּי אֲסִירַ֙יִךְ֙ מִבּ֔וֹר אֵ֥ין מַ֖יִם בּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: As for you also, because of the blood of your covenant, I have sent forth your prisoners out of the pit in which there is no water.

notes.official: *gam-ʾatt bəḏam-bərîṯēḵ* 'As for you also, because of the blood of your covenant' (cf. Ex 24:8). *šillaḥtî ʾăsîrayiḵ mibbôr ʾên mayim bô* 'I have sent forth your prisoners out of the pit in which there is no water': the dry cistern used as a prison, as for Joseph (Gen 37:24) and Jeremiah (Jer 38:6) (central `bor-pit-cistern-dry-water-shaft`).

paragraphs.text: שׁ֚וּבוּ לְבִצָּר֔וֹן אֲסִירֵ֖י הַתִּקְוָ֑ה גַּם־הַיּ֕וֹם מַגִּ֥יד מִשְׁנֶ֖ה אָשִׁ֥יב לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: Return to the stronghold, you prisoners of hope; even today I declare that I will restore double to you.

notes.official: *ʾăsîrê hattiqwâ* 'you prisoners of hope'; *mišneh ʾāšîḇ lāḵ* 'I will restore double to you' (cf. Isa 61:7).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־דָרַ֨כְתִּי לִ֜י יְהוּדָ֗ה קֶ֚שֶׁת מִלֵּ֣אתִי אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְעוֹרַרְתִּ֤י בָנַ֙יִךְ֙ צִיּ֔וֹן עַל־בָּנַ֖יִךְ יָוָ֑ן וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךְ כְּחֶ֥רֶב גִּבּֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: For I have bent Judah for me, I have filled the bow with Ephraim; and I will stir up your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and will make you like the sword of a mighty man.

notes.official: *kî-ḏāraḵtî lî yəhûḏâ qešeṯ millēʾṯî ʾep̄rayim* 'For I have bent Judah for me, I have filled the bow with Ephraim': Judah is the bow and Ephraim the arrow. *ʿal-bānayiḵ yāwān* 'against your sons, Greece': *yāwān* (Ionia) is rendered by its English name, as in daniel-woh; Gen 10:2 'Javan' is the same word (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zechariah-4-5-9`).

paragraphs.text: וַֽיהוָה֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם יֵֽרָאֶ֔ה וְיָצָ֥א כַבָּרָ֖ק חִצּ֑וֹ וַֽאדֹנָ֤י יְהֹוִה֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֣ר יִתְקָ֔ע וְהָלַ֖ךְ בְּסַעֲר֥וֹת תֵּימָֽן׃

i18n.en: And YHWH shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth like the lightning; and the Lord YHWH will blow the shofar, and will go with whirlwinds of the south.

notes.official: *wayhwh ʿălêhem yērāʾeh* 'And YHWH shall be seen over them': the divine warrior appears in the storm, his arrow 'like the lightning' (Ps 18:15; Hab 3:11). *waʾḏōnāy YHWH baššôp̄ār yiṯqāʿ* 'and the Lord YHWH will blow the shofar' (central `adonai-yhwh`; `shofar-latter-prophets`), replacing the draft's ASV 'trumpet'; the source points the name *yəhōwih*. *bəsaʿărôṯ têmān* 'with whirlwinds of the south': *têmān* is 'the south', and also the Edomite region from which YHWH comes in the old theophany poems (Hab 3:3; Judg 5:4). The line keeps the ASV (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zechariah-4-5-9`).

paragraphs.text: יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֮ יָגֵ֣ן עֲלֵיהֶם֒ וְאָכְל֗וּ וְכָֽבְשׁוּ֙ אַבְנֵי־קֶ֔לַע וְשָׁת֥וּ הָמ֖וּ כְּמוֹ־יָ֑יִן וּמָֽלְאוּ֙ כַּמִּזְרָ֔ק כְּזָוִיּ֖וֹת מִזְבֵּֽחַ׃

i18n.en: YHWH of hosts will defend them; and they shall devour, and shall tread down the sling-stones; and they shall drink and make a noise as through wine; and they shall be filled like bowls, like the corners of the altar.

notes.official: *YHWH ṣəḇāʾôṯ yāḡēn ʿălêhem* 'YHWH of hosts will defend them' (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`). *wəʾāḵəlû wəḵāḇəšû ʾaḇnê-qelaʿ wəšāṯû hāmû kəmô-yāyin* 'and they shall devour, and shall tread down the sling-stones; and they shall drink and make a noise as through wine': the clauses are obscure, an image of victors in a battle frenzy. The Old Greek reads 'they shall drink their blood like wine', and the MT is kept (`mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-zechariah-4-5-9`). *ûmālʾû kammizrāq kəzāwiyyôṯ mizbēaḥ* 'and they shall be filled like bowls, like the corners of the altar', drenched as the sacrificial bowls and the altar's corners are with blood (central `mizbeach-olah`).

paragraphs.text: וְֽהוֹשִׁיעָ֞ם יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כְּצֹ֣אן עַמּ֑וֹ כִּ֚י אַבְנֵי־נֵ֔זֶר מִֽתְנוֹסְס֖וֹת עַל־אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And YHWH their God will save them on that day as the flock of his people; for they shall be like the stones of a crown, lifted on high over his ground.

notes.official: *wəhôšîʿām YHWH ʾĕlōhêhem* 'And YHWH their God will save them' (`elohim-god-latter-prophets`). *kî ʾaḇnê-nēzer miṯnôsəsôṯ ʿal-ʾaḏmāṯô* 'for they shall be like the stones of a crown, lifted on high over his ground': *miṯnôsəsôṯ* is from *nēs* 'banner' ('lifted on high', ASV) or means 'sparkling' (NRSV); *ʾaḏmāṯô* 'his ground' (central `adam-adamah`; ASV 'his land') (overlay `lexical-cruxes-zechariah-4-5-9`).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֥י מַה־טּוּב֖וֹ וּמַה־יָפְי֑וֹ דָּגָן֙ בַּֽחוּרִ֔ים וְתִיר֖וֹשׁ יְנוֹבֵ֥ב בְּתֻלֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty! Grain shall make the young men flourish, and new wine the maidens.

notes.official: *kî mah-ṭûḇô ûmah-yop̄yô* 'For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty!': 'his' may refer to YHWH, the people or the land, and the line leaves it open, as the Hebrew does. *dāḡān* 'grain' and *tîrôš* 'new wine' are two of the three harvest goods, the third being *yiṣhār* (Deut 7:13; cf. 4:14).
